clue.text: Incantation in 9, but not mumbo jumbo

definitions.text: Incantation in 9, but not mumbo jumbo

parts.words: Incantation in 9, but not mumbo jumbo
parts.note: 9 is the answer to 9 down, so this is a magic formula in rhyming form, a nonsense phrase of the conjuror's kind, though not the other rhyming term named

explanation.surface: A spell is described as being in verse yet not mere gibberish.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 9 down points at a rhyme: the answer is a rhyming conjuror's phrase, and mumbo-jumbo, another rhyming jingle for nonsense, is waved away as the wrong one.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjuror's patter word used while performing tricks, a mock spell.

clue.text: Off limits, like an exhausted kangaroo?

definitions.meaning: a kangaroo too tired to keep hopping has used up its leaps

explanation.surface: A tired kangaroo is somewhere it should not be.
explanation.definitionFit: Forbidden territory; whimsically, having no leaps left.

clue.text: Distant, and powerless to hold train up

indicators.note: the word for powerless contains the reversed word

parts.note: unable means powerless to do something

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to train a gun is to aim it

explanation.surface: Someone aloof and unable to lift a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' is the verb, to point a gun, not a railway train; 'up' reads it upwards in this down clue, and 'to hold' puts the result inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfriendly and standoffish, so aloof in manner.

clue.text: Fuss over British plant

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: pother is an old word for a commotion or fuss

explanation.surface: A commotion over a plant from Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A leafy vegetable or herb grown for the cooking pot.

clue.text: On high perch, perhaps, weep and disparage one's own efforts

parts.note: to cry is to weep
fish that is high is rotten and smelly, and perch is an example of a fish

explanation.surface: Someone up on a lofty perch sobs and belittles their own work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' means going off, smelly, as with game or fish; a perch is a fish, not a roost.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to run down one's own goods or achievements.

clue.text: Cutting thus, limiting girl's rise

indicators.note: the word for thus encloses the reversed name

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus

indicators.note: in a down clue the girl's name goes upwards, so is reversed

parts.note: Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Restricting a young woman's promotion is described as hurtful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thus' is the Latin word editors use to mark a quoted error; 'rise' reads the girl's name upwards in this down clue, and 'limiting' encloses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocking and sarcastic, as cutting remarks are.

clue.text: Foremost of those shot after revolution

definitions.text: Foremost of those shot after revolution

parts.words: Foremost of those shot after revolution
parts.note: the Russian emperor Nicholas II was the leading figure among the family killed by the Bolsheviks in 1918

explanation.surface: Someone at the front of a group shot following an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foremost of' tempts a first-letter pick, but the whole clue describes the last Russian emperor, executed with his family after the 1917 revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian emperor was the most prominent of the victims killed at Yekaterinburg.

clue.text: Act like Bunter and express derision

definitions.meaning: Billy Bunter, the greedy fat schoolboy of British comic stories, gobbles food

explanation.surface: Imitating a famous schoolboy by sneering.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Bunter is a gluttonous schoolboy from old British children's stories.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat greedily; also to jeer contemptuously.

clue.text: Recital of Frost's verse

indicators.note: a recital is spoken aloud, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: rime is hoar frost

explanation.surface: A reading of a poem by Robert Frost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frost' suggests the poet, but it is rime, white frost.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetry with matching end sounds, a synonym for verse.

clue.text: Secretive way to replace head in fine form

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word for fine form is swapped out for the abbreviation for way

parts.note: in fine form means fit and well, healthy
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A covert method of getting a head into good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace head in' puts ST in place of the H at the front of HEALTHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe acting quietly and furtively so as not to be noticed.

clue.text: Speculative view of ambassador held by politician

indicators.note: the ambassador's abbreviation is contained within the word for the politician

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative politician
HE stands for His Excellency, the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: A diplomat's conjecture is adopted by a party member.
explanation.walkthrough: His Excellency is the formal address for an ambassador; a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party, and 'held by' puts the title inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypothesis or conjecture is a speculative idea not yet proved.

clue.text: Function of cricket side, one assembled by church

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field
I is the Roman numeral for one
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The purpose of a cricket team, one gathered together by a church.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the off side is the half of the field facing the batsman's bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A role or duty one performs is a post or position held, a synonym sense.

clue.text: Frenchman entitled to make allowance for weight when carrying rock

indicators.note: the word for the weight allowance holds the rock within it

parts.note: tare is the deduction made for the weight of packaging or container
tuff is a rock formed from volcanic ash

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is permitted to allow for the weight of rock he is lugging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entitled' means named in a title: Molière's comedy is named after this hypocrite.
explanation.definitionFit: Molière's play about a religious hypocrite takes its title from this French character.

clue.text: Make drink, passing over servants? That's a bloomer.

parts.note: to forge is to make or shape

indicators.note: the drink goes around, passing over, the servants

parts.note: a tot is a small drink
men can mean servants or workers

explanation.surface: Brew a drink and skip the staff; that's a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder; it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A small blue flower, so something that blooms.

clue.text: Thoroughly search for source of honey

definitions.meaning: to go through an area minutely, as with a fine-toothed implement
the wax cells of a hive in which bees store honey

explanation.surface: A thorough hunt for where honey comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to search meticulously; the other is the honey-holding wax structure of a hive.

clue.text: Endless luck, as robin flying around is seen in these?

definitions.text: Endless luck, as robin flying around is seen in these?

indicators.note: the letters are sent whirling into a new order, like a bird in flight
the word luck is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: With some good fortune a birdwatcher spots a robin through field glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' drops the last letter of luck, and 'flying around' scrambles the pool. The whole clue also pictures a birdwatcher spotting a robin through field glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Field glasses are what a birdwatcher views a flying robin through.

clue.text: Napier's invention to record an aspect of music heard

parts.note: a log is a record

indicators.note: the phrase is to be spoken, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: a rhythm is one element of music

explanation.surface: A Scottish mathematician's device for noting a musical feature.
explanation.walkthrough: John Napier introduced these in 1614; 'a rhythm' heard aloud gives ARITHM.
explanation.definitionFit: Napier devised these exponents to simplify multiplication.

clue.text: Bold undertaking, to enrol in force

parts.note: to enter a competition or school is to enrol in it
to prise something open is to force it

explanation.surface: Joining the armed forces is presented as a daring venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' looks like the armed services, but it is a verb: to lever open.
explanation.definitionFit: A daring venture or initiative undertaken with spirit.

clue.text: Charges embroiling northern royals

indicators.note: the charges word takes the abbreviation into its middle

parts.note: prices are charges

explanation.surface: Accusations involving northern members of the monarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sons of a monarch are members of a royal family.

clue.text: Prohibition makes 'em move beyond normal drinking environment

indicators.note: the word for move comes after the other pieces

parts.note: the 'em of the clue gives its letters as written
a bar is where one usually drinks
to go is to move

explanation.surface: A ban forces drinkers to go elsewhere than the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: An official ban on trade is a prohibition.

clue.text: Information about lake in narrow valley

indicators.note: the word for information goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Facts concerning a lake lying in a narrow valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish word for a steep, narrow valley.

clue.text: Arrogant fool with posh china

parts.note: an ass is a fool
U means upper-class, posh
Ming is a type of fine Chinese porcelain

explanation.surface: An idiot who owns expensive porcelain.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old label for upper-class usage, so 'posh'.
explanation.definitionFit: Presumptuous and haughty, taking too much upon oneself.

clue.text: Acknowledge head 'of metro in underground passage

indicators.note: the leading letter goes inside the passage word

parts.note: an adit is a horizontal mine entrance

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Admit the leader of the subway is in a tunnel.
explanation.definitionFit: To confess or concede something is true.

clue.text: Was present as visitor weaved fabric

parts.note: sat means was present, sitting
to sit in on something is to attend as a visitor

explanation.surface: A guest attended while cloth was woven.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'sit in' on a class or meeting is to attend as an observer.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth glossy woven cloth.

clue.text: Ancient vessel put together by, say, military engineers

indicators.note: the word by is to be heard spoken, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: the spoken word by is spelt differently here
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: An old ship assembled by army engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks a homophone of 'by', spelt BI; REME is a British Army engineering corps.
explanation.definitionFit: A galley of classical times with two banks of oars.

clue.text: Like the arrangement of feet concealed in some tricycles

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Something about pedals hidden away among a few children's bikes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feet' are metrical feet, units of rhythm in verse, not the feet that pedal a tricycle.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to metre, the pattern of stressed and unstressed syllables in poetry.

clue.text: Quietly abandons train trip, somehow creating annoyance

indicators.note: signals that the remaining letters are put together in some new way
the letter for quietly is dropped from the phrase train trip

parts.note: taken as written
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone quietly gives up a rail journey, causing irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandons' drops P from TRAIN TRIP to leave TRAINTRI, which 'somehow' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing that causes irritation, a source of annoyance.

clue.text: Temporary accommodation for wine

definitions.meaning: a canvas shelter used for camping
a deep red Spanish wine, often used as communion wine

explanation.surface: A short-term lodging offered for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A camper's canvas shelter; also an old name for a dark red Spanish wine.

clue.text: Fish's companion? Possibly one in the same stream

definitions.meaning: a fellow member of a shoal of fish
a fellow pupil in the same ability group at a British school

explanation.surface: A fish swimming with another in the same river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stream' is the British school term for a class grouped by ability, not a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow pupil; read playfully, a fellow member of a shoal.
